name: AnimatedList
description: A list whose items slide and fade in one after another, and stack as new ones are added. It is a real list (ul with li items), and every item is in the page from the start.

children.description: The items. Each child becomes one list item; give each a stable key so only genuinely new items animate.

delay.description: Seconds between one item appearing and the next, for items that arrive together.

duration.description: Seconds each item takes to slide in.

announce.description: Marks the list as a polite live region so screen readers announce items that are added later. Leave it off for a static list.

isStill.description: Shows every item at once with no movement. Moving content should be stoppable.

requirements: A real list: ul with one li per item, so the item count is announced
Every item is real DOM in the server HTML and visible without JavaScript or CSS animation
Stands still for visitors who ask for less motion (prefers-reduced-motion), and with isStill or inside an rdm-still container
Each item moves once and stops, so nothing keeps moving and nothing flashes (WCAG 2.2.2, 2.3.1)
Items keep their own focus order and content; the animation never moves focus
Optional: it is a separate component, so projects that do not add it carry none of its code
screenReader: Read as a list with its number of items
With announce on, items added later are read out politely, once, without interrupting

use_when: A feed or activity log where new entries arrive
A short list that should feel built up rather than dropped in
avoid_when: Long lists: staggered delays make the last items wait
Lists people scan quickly or sort and filter often
anti_patterns: A delay so long that content is hidden for several seconds
Turning on announce for a list that changes every second
